@Fiendish-Beaver At least it sounds like Gears may have done better than the 300,000 copies sold that some were saying.
It was above Galactic Racer, which had 1.5 million players.
A few thousand may not have played it day one, but surely not 265,000 players?
Now, is 400k a good result on its own for a game that cost at least $300 million to make (with some estimates putting it a lot more than that)?

The problem though comes down to simple maths, if E-Day cost $200 million (and bear in mind that is a conservative figure because we are led to believe it cost much more than that to make), but still, if it cost $200 million to make, then the game needs to sell the equivalent of 2,850,000 full priced games in order to just break even, and it is a long way short of that in sheer sales.

Gears of War E-Day has sold well on Xbox because:

1) Asha said, "It enjoyed a strong start".
3) The Premium Edition ($100) has been higher in the ranking, ahead of Standard and Upgrade.

As I have said before, the problem is that the game needs to retain a sizable number of daily players, and judging by Steam alone, which saw just 2,978 players in the past 24 hours, which is a drop of more than 90% in little over a month, then E-Day is not retaining its players.
